title: What happens if you open your helmet in space?

lines.say: What happens if you open your helmet in space? Do you explode?
Good news. You don't explode. Your skin is tough enough to hold you together.
The bad news? With no oxygen, you'd have about fifteen seconds before you pass out.
The spit on your tongue would start to bubble and boil, because the pressure is so low.
And never hold your breath. The air in your lungs would expand and hurt them.
But if you're pulled back inside within about ninety seconds, you'd probably survive.
This really happened. In 1966, a NASA test suit leaked inside a vacuum chamber. The engineer passed out in about fifteen seconds, and woke up just fine.
